Photograph: Wikimedia View image in fullscreen Adani will pay no tax this financial year despite generating about $1bn in revenue from coal mining in Queensland. Photograph: Wikimedia Adani Group Adani to pay no company tax despite $1bn revenue from Queensland coalmine Indian conglomerate offsets earnings from Carmichael mine to report $340.6m loss, after promising billions in taxes and royalties Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Jonathan Barrett Business editor Fri 31 Jul 2026 20.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 22.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Indian conglomerate Adani will pay no company tax despite generating almost $1bn in revenue from coal mining in Queensland over the past year. Financial accounts show the Carmichael thermal coal operations used large costs – including production and related party logistics expenses – to offset its $963.5m revenue in the 12 months to 31 March. This resulted in a recorded $340.6m loss for the year, erasing its tax bill. Guardian Australia analysis of company accounts shows the mining project has never paid corporate tax after opening in 2021, despite past pledges by Adani that the operations would plough billions of dollars in taxes and royalties into the economy. Adani donated $600,000 to Liberal National party before 2024 state election using federal ‘loophole’ Read more Adani Mining’s accounts show that it paid $58m in royalties in the 12-month period. Royalties are payments made to governments to extract state-owned minerals. Adani also paid a $33.1m royalty to a related party. Tim Buckley, a former investment banker and the director of Climate Energy Finance, said the company was structured so that it wouldn’t pay corporate tax in Australia. “This is a perfect example of why Australia needs new rules that ensure foreign entities have a sensible capital structure,” said Buckley, who advocates for changes that would limit the amount of deductions a business can make to reduce tax. Adani’s project approval in central Queensland’s Galilee Basin was fiercely contested , opening a new jurisdiction of thermal coal extraction that raised environmental concerns. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Industry groups supporting the conglomerate had claimed Adani’s project would fund schools, hospitals and other infrastructure for “almost a century” through mining taxes and royalties. A spokesperson for Adani Mining said the project provided direct jobs for more than 1,400 Queenslanders last financial year. “We comply fully with our state and commonwealth taxation and royalty obligations and our statutory profit and tax outcomes are determined in accordance with Australian accounting standards and the corporations act,” the spokesperson said. The Carmichael operations opened during a prosperous time for coalminers. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine sent global energy prices soaring in 2022. Coal prices are now also being supported by energy supply constraints caused by conflict in the Middle East. The Adani-controlled Abbot Point port business, named North Queensland Export Terminal, also did not pay any company tax over the most recent 12-month reporting period, despite earning $356.6m. Various operating expenses lead to a $6.8m loss, with no tax payable. The terminal business’s chief executive, Mark Smith, said accounts were prepared in accordance with Australian accounting standards and reflect the capital-intensive nature of owning and operating major export infrastructure. “The terminal plays an important role in supporting Queensland trade and we remain focused on delivering safe, reliable, and efficient export services for our customers,” Smith said. https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/v.text: Vietnam has approved its National Digital Transformation Strategy for 2026–30, which sets out a long-term plan to build a data‑ and AI‑driven digital nation by 2045.The strategy, issued under Decision 1266/QD‑TTg, puts people and businesses at the center of digital transformation and positions digital technologies as a core engine of economic growth. Deputy Prime Minister Ho Quoc Dung approved the plan, reports Vietnam News.The government aims to fully digitalize administrative records by 2030, achieve 99 per cent satisfaction with online public services and ensure all ministries and provinces use shared national digital platforms.Key databases will be standardized and interconnected. Provincial smart operation centers will be upgraded with AI for forecasting, monitoring and decision support. Every public servant will receive digital skills training and an AI assistant account.The strategy targets a digital economy contributing at least 30 per cent of GDP by 2030. At least 500,000 SMEs will receive digital transformation support; e‑commerce will reach up to 17 per cent of retail sales, and cashless payments will expand to 30 times GDP. Secure national data exchanges will be established, and more than 40 per cent of SMEs are expected to adopt AI‑based services.To narrow the digital divide, fibre‑optic broadband will be extended to all households; 95 per cent of people aged 15 and above will hold bank or financial accounts, and electronic health records will cover the entire population. Ten million working‑age people will receive basic digital skills training.Data is defined as a strategic national resource. The government plans a unified data governance framework and an integrated national database incorporating AI to support policymaking and service delivery. Priority databases include population, land, business, finance, healthcare, education and social security.The strategy also emphasizes building a competitive “Make in Vietnam” digital technology ecosystem. Domestic tech firms will be supported through public procurement, regulatory sandboxes and investment. Funding is prioritized for R&D, cybersecurity, cloud, semiconductors and digital platforms. The government encourages collaboration across enterprises, universities and research institutes to strengthen national digital value chains.Broadens digital ID platform to support public services, secure transactionsVietnam is growing its national digital identity ambitions with a new government resolution that broadens its role in public services and digital transactions.The upgraded platform will give citizens access to their digital data and offer free digital signature certification for use in online administrative procedures. In addition, it will provide electronic identification and authentication.It will also support online public service delivery, enable electronic submission of documents, link payment accounts for public service and social security transactions, and serve as a secure communication channel between citizens, government and businesses.The Ministry of Public Security’s Department of Administrative Management of Social Order has been assigned to operate and further develop the national digital identity system. The Government has also designated October 15 as Vietnam Digital Citizen Day to promote awareness and adoption.The resolution takes effect from August 15 through February 28, 2027.Vietnam’s VNeID digital ID system has surpassed 102 million identity records and 71.5 million activated accounts. The country has looked to Estonian e-governance experts for digital identity and data unification experience in a bilateral exchange.

But It's Not New Marko Nguyen Aug 22 5 mins read Sponsored Share this post X LinkedIn Email Facebook Copy link TL;DR One UI 9 (Android 17) stable is live on Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, rolling out to S26 in August Now Nudge AI watches your screen and suggests contextual shortcuts in real time Gemini-powered Galaxy AI handles multi-step tasks through a single voice command 49 Galaxy devices are in internal testing, including Galaxy A-series budget phones Beta is available through the Samsung Members app for Galaxy S26 users in six countries Samsung pushed the stable One UI 9 build to Galaxy Z Fold 8 devices globally this week, and 49 more Galaxy devices are in internal testing for the Android 17-based update. This isn’t a cosmetic refresh — One UI 9 introduces contextual AI features that fundamentally change how Samsung phones interact with you. The biggest addition, Now Nudge, actively monitors what’s on your screen and serves helpful shortcuts before you ask for them. Samsung Galaxy S26 Available on Amazon Galaxy AI, powerful performance, and immersive viewing with a durable battery for everyday use. Check Price Now Nudge Turns Your Screen Into an AI Trigger The headline feature of One UI 9 is Now Nudge , an AI system that watches on-screen activity and pops up contextual action cards at the right moment. Text a friend about dinner plans? Now Nudge suggests opening your calendar, pulling up a restaurant app, or setting a reminder — without you opening anything manually. This is Samsung’s most aggressive AI integration yet. Previous Galaxy AI features like Circle to Search and Live Translate were tools you activated deliberately. Now Nudge flips that model: the phone decides when to offer help. Whether that feels useful or intrusive will depend on Samsung’s sensitivity calibration, but early beta testers have reported the suggestions feel surprisingly accurate rather than annoying. Now Nudge also feeds into a new AI Assistant Activity Dashboard , giving you a centralized view of every AI automation running on your behalf. You can review, pause, or dismiss any suggestion from one screen. That transparency matters because users need to trust an always-watching AI system, and Samsung clearly anticipated the privacy concern. Gemini-Powered Galaxy AI Handles Multi-Step Tasks Samsung deepened its Gemini Intelligence partnership with Google in One UI 9, and the results show up across the OS. The new Gemini-powered Galaxy AI lets you complete multiple actions through a single natural-language request. Ask Gemini to “find my flight confirmation, add it to my calendar, and share the details with Mom,” and it chains those actions without you switching apps. Additionally, Samsung introduced Gemini Notebook — a dedicated space where Gemini can draft, edit, and organize notes using voice or text input. It integrates with Samsung Notes, syncing content bidirectionally so you can start a note in Notebook and finish it in the full Notes app. Updated Quick Panel and notification system The visual overhaul is subtler but functional. Samsung redesigned the Quick Settings panel with cleaner borderless circular toggles that replace the old rectangular tiles. The notification shade now groups alerts by priority with smarter sorting — high-priority messages surface first, while app promotions get buried. The settings menu also got restructured to reduce tap depth. Common adjustments that previously required three or four taps now take two. It’s a small change, but it compounds over dozens of daily interactions. Which Apps Got Updated With One UI 9 Several Samsung apps received significant overhauls alongside the system update. Samsung Notes now supports real-time collaboration and AI-powered text summarization — paste a long article, and Notes generates a bullet-point summary instantly. The Gallery app improved its search with natural-language queries. Samsung Internet gained better tab management and tracking protection . For foldable users, Samsung refined multitasking gestures and app continuity between cover and main screens. The handoff that occasionally stuttered on the Z Fold 7 runs more smoothly, with apps maintaining their exact scroll position during transitions. How to Get the One UI 9 Beta on Your Galaxy Phone The beta is available through Samsung Members for eligible devices. Open the Samsung Members app, tap the One UI 9 Beta banner on the home screen, accept the terms, then go to Settings > Software update > Download and install . The beta firmware appears as an available update. Currently, the beta is live for Galaxy S26 series users in the U.S., U.K., Germany, India, Korea, and Poland, with the Galaxy S25 series added in mid-August. If the banner doesn’t appear, your device or region isn’t eligible yet. Important: Back up your data before enrolling. You can roll back to stable One UI 8.5 through Samsung Members, but the rollback wipes your device. Samsung Galaxy S26 Available on Amazon Galaxy AI, powerful performance, and immersive viewing with a durable battery for everyday use. Check Price 49 Devices in Testing — When Is Your Phone Getting It? Samsung’s software rollout roadmap splits devices into monthly (flagships) and quarterly (mid-range) update tiers. Here’s when each device group gets One UI 9, based on internal testing data and Samsung’s published schedule: Phase Timeline Devices Tier 1 July 2026 Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, Z Flip 8 Pre-installed 2 Aug 2026 Galaxy S26, S26+, S26 Ultra Monthly 3 Aug–Sep 2026 Galaxy S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 FE, Z Fold 7, Z Flip 7, Z TriFold Monthly 4 Sep–Oct 2026 Galaxy S24, S24+, S24 Ultra, S24 FE, Z Fold 6, Z Flip 6, Z Fold 5, Z Flip 5 Monthly 5 Oct–Nov 2026 Galaxy S23, S23+, S23 Ultra, S23 FE, A56 5G, A55 5G, A54 5G, Tab S11, Tab S10 FE Monthly 6 Nov–Dec 2026 Galaxy A57, A37, A27, A17, A07, M56, M36, M16, F56, C55, Tab A11, Tab A9+ Quarterly 7 Late 2026+ Galaxy A73, A53, A34, A25, A16, A06, M55, M35, M15, F55, F35, Tab S9, Tab S8 Quarterly Devices on the monthly tier — all S-series (S23–S26), Z Fold/Flip (3–8), and W-series — get security patches and major updates first. Quarterly devices follow on a staggered schedule. The surprise is how many budget Galaxy A phones made the list — even the A07 is in testing, suggesting Samsung is accelerating Android 17 delivery to millions of affordable Galaxy users . FAQs What is Now Nudge in One UI 9? Now Nudge is a contextual AI feature that monitors your screen activity and suggests relevant shortcuts in real time. For example, it might suggest opening your calendar when you text about upcoming plans, or pull up a related app without manual input. How do I install the One UI 9 beta? Open the Samsung Members app, tap the One UI 9 Beta banner, accept terms, then go to Settings > Software update > Download and install. The beta is currently available for Galaxy S26 and S25 series in the U.S., U.K., Germany, India, Korea, and Poland. Which Samsung phones will get One UI 9? Samsung is testing One UI 9 on 49 devices, including the Galaxy S23 through S26, Z Fold 5 through Z Fold 8, and Galaxy A models down to the budget Galaxy A07 . Stable rollout runs from August through December 2026. What’s new in Samsung apps with One UI 9? Samsung Notes gained AI-powered summarization and real-time collaboration. Samsung Health improved Galaxy Watch integration. The Gallery app now supports natural-language photo search, and Samsung Internet added better tab management . Will the Galaxy A-series get One UI 9? Yes. Samsung is internally testing One UI 9 on Galaxy A57, A37, A27, A17, and even the A07. This is the broadest mid-range testing list Samsung has released for a major Android update, suggesting faster rollout than previous years. Photograph: imac/Alamy Mississippi Two white students at University of Mississippi make monkey gestures in Ring video Women are reportedly upstairs neighbors of three Black students, including one who uploaded video to TikTok Uwa Ede-Osifo Tue 10 Nov 2026 21.26 EST Last modified on Tue 10 Nov 2026 21.51 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Two white students at the University of Mississippi were captured making offensive monkey gestures in a widely panned Ring video that has prompted a school investigation . On Saturday, freshman Jakiyra Metcalf uploaded the surveillance clip from her apartment door to TikTok, showing one woman thumping her chest and babbling like a monkey. Another woman jumped into the camera’s view and mimicked the primate noises. The video, which has nearly 13m views, drew outrage over the racist connotation. “This is absolutely disgusting and unacceptable. College is supposed to be a place where young adults can learn, grow, and feel safe,” Metcalf’s mother, Tasha Bolton, wrote Saturday on Facebook. According to Bolton, her daughter lives with two Black roommates and the women seen in the video are her upstairs neighbors. The family is not yet speaking publicly about the ordeal, said Bolton’s husband, Brooks Bolton. Alaina Kunes, 18, who was in the video, issued an apology in a statement released by a Chicago law firm, while insisting her behavior was not related to race. “I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color,” Kunes said. “I have apologized to the women, and I pray they will forgive me.” Kunes continued: “Over the past several days, my family and I have received death threats and harassment. I am grateful for the authorities working to ensure our safety. As I intend to cooperate fully with the University’s investigation, I ask for privacy for my family. I understand the seriousness of this situation and remain committed to taking responsibility and learning from this embarrassing ordeal.” Shawnboda Mead, vice-chancellor for student affairs at the university, condemned the video in a Sunday statement. “Every student deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued at the University of Mississippi . Racism and actions that disparage people because of an aspect of their identity have no place in our campus community,” she said. Mead also advised the campus to refrain from sharing unverified information about who was involved in the incident. The school has reached out to the affected students to offer support and hear their concerns, she said. A university spokesperson did not reply to a Tuesday inquiry about the women’s enrollment status and whether any disciplinary action had been taken. The school has seen troubling incidents of racism in the past. In 2014, fraternity members at the University of Mississippi hung a noose around a statue that commemorated the school’s first Black student. A decade later , at a pro-Palestine demonstration, some white male counter-protesters directed monkey noises at a Black female protester.
